GOVERNMENT OF INDIA  
MINISTRY OF COOPERATION  
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1248 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 11th FEBRUARY, 2025 
 
World's Largest Grain Storage Plans 
 
1248. Shri Dushyant Singh: 
 
Will the Minister of Cooperation (सहकारिता मंत्री) be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the details of the total number of co -operative societies currently functioning in the 
country, State and District-wise; 
(b)  whether the Government has established any mechanism to monitor the functioning of 
Co-operative societies, and if so, the details of this monitoring framework, including any 
oversight authorities and procedures; 
(c)  the details of actions being taken by the Government to ensure that all co -operative 
societies undergo annual audits and the manner in which the Government is promoting 
accountability and transparency within these organizations; and 
(d)  the details of the 'World’s Largest Grain Storage Plan of the Government in the 
Cooperative Sector, including its budget outlay, primary objectives and the expected 
advantages particularly in addressing foodgrain storage challenges? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF COOPERATION 
सहकारिता मंत्री (SHRI AMIT SHAH) 
 
(a): As per National Cooperative Database there are more than 8 lakh cooperative societies 
in the country, out of which total 6,28,398 cooperative societies are currently function al, 
covering various sectors such as Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS), Dairy, Fishery, 
Housing, and Multi -purpose Cooperatives. The State -wise and District -wise details are 
enclosed at Annexure-I and Annexure-II respectively. 
 
(b) The monitoring of cooperative societies is primarily handled by the respective State/UT 
Governments, as they are responsible for overseeing their registration, functioning, and 
compliance. However, the Ministry of Cooperation has introduced several mec hanisms to 
improve oversight and governance. The computerization of PACS has been a significant step 
toward ensuring transparency in financial transactions. Additionally, a National Cooperative 
Database has been  developed to create a centralized system for  tracking the status and 
performance of cooperatives across the country. The enactment of the Multi-State Cooperative 
Societies (Amendment) Act, 2023, has further strengthened governance by introducing 
stringent regulations, improved accountability standards, and increased transpa rency in the 
functioning of multi-state cooperative societies. Institutions such as NABARD and NCDC are 

also playing a crucial role in policy guidance, financial support, and capacity -building 
initiatives to improve cooperative governance. 
 
(c) The audit of cooperative societies is a critical aspect of ensuring financial discipline 
and accountability, and it comes under the purview of  the respective State/UT Governments 
under their Cooperative Acts. Further, to ensure the timely and accurate audit of PACS, online 
audit is being conducted by States/ UT under Computerization of PACS Project, enabling real-
time financial reporting and reducing irregularities.  
 
The project for Computerization of functional PACS has been approved by the Government of 
India with a total financial outlay of ₹2,516 Crore, and it entails bringing all functional PACS 
in the country onto a n ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning) based common national software 
which aims to improve their operational efficiency, ensure speedy disbursal of loans, lower 
transaction costs and increase transparency. 
 
(d) In order to address the foodgrain storage challenges in rural areas , the Government on 
31.05.2023, has approved the “World’s Largest Grain Storage Plan in Cooperative Sector”, 
which has been rolled out as a Pilot Project. The Plan entails creation of various agri 
infrastructure at PACS level, including godowns, custom hir ing center, processing units, Fair 
Price Shops, etc. through convergence of various existing schemes of the Government of India 
(GoI), such as, Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF), Ag ricultural Marketing Infrastructure 
Scheme (AMI), Sub Mission on Agricultural Mechanization (SMAM) Pradhan Mantri 
Formalization of Micro Food Processing Enterprises Scheme (PMFME), etc. Under the Pilot 
Project of the Plan, construction of godowns has been completed in 11 PACS of 11 States . 
Foundation Stone has been laid in 500 PACS of 10 States. 
 
This plan is being implemented by utilizing the existing budgetary outlays under various 
Government of India schemes, such as AIF, AMI, SMAM, etc., that are being converged at the 
level of these primary level cooperative societies. 
 
The objective of the initiative is to establish grain storage infrastructure at the PACS level to 
decentralize storage, reduce post-harvest losses, and enhance food security. This plan enables 
PACS to act as procurement and storage hubs, improving their ec onomic viability while 
strengthening rural food supply chains. The initiative intends to reduce foodgrain wastage, cut 
transportation costs for farmers, and ensure better price realization, thus improving overall 
market efficiency and financial sustainabil ity of PACS. By empowering cooperatives with 
modern storage infrastructure, this initiative aims to transform rural agricultural supply chains 
and create long-term economic benefits for farmers.
